{{Short description|American statistician}}
{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=March 2024}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=March 2024}}
'''Susan M. Hinkins''' is a retired American government and survey statistician who has worked for the [[Internal Revenue Service]], the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]], [[Ernst & Young]], [[NORC at the University of Chicago]], and multiple [[human rights]] organizations.{{r|hrdag}}

==Education and career==
Hinkins majored in mathematics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], graduating in 1971. She went to [[Montana State University]], where she earned a master's degree in mathematics in 1973,{{r|hrdag|cobell}} and completed a Ph.D. in statistics in 1979. Her doctoral dissertation, '' Using Incomplete Multivariate Data to Simultaneously Estimate the Means'', was supervised by Martin Alva Hamilton.{{r|mg}}

She began her government service in 1980–1981, working for the Office of Radiation Programs of the United States Environmental Protection Agency, on the measurement of [[radon]] in homes.{{r|hrdag|cobell}} Next, she worked for the Internal Revenue Service from 1981 to 1998, on income statistics.  After three years at Ernst & Young, working on [[quality of service]] in [[telecommunications]],{{r|hrdag}} she joined NORC as a senior statistician in 2001.{{r|norc}} At NORC, she managed accounting data for Native American funds held by the US government,{{r|hrdag}} and testified as an expert in the [[Cobell v. Salazar]] lawsuit concerning alleged mismanagement of those funds.{{r|cobell}} Her other work at NORC concerned household survey data, anonymization of medicare data, and the assessment of capabilities for rapid response to [[bioterrorism]].{{r|hrdag}} While continuing at NORC as a senior statistician, she also chaired the committee on scientific freedom and human rights of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA),{{r|somers-ham}} served as advisor to the scientific advisory committee of the [[Human Rights Data Analysis Group]] from 2013 to 2021,{{r|hrdag}} represented the ASA on the Science and Human Rights Coalition of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS),{{r|shrc}} and co-chaired the AAAS Service to the Human Rights Community working group.{{r|wg}}

==Personal life==
Hinkins is the daughter of Russell Hinkins (1901–1988), a high school teacher and principal, farmer, and grain storage official in southwestern Wisconsin.{{r|russell}}
She has worked as a dance instructor for [[Scottish country dance]] in [[Bozeman, Montana]].{{r|dance}}

==Recognition==
Hinkins was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2004.{{r|fasa}}
